Selected preparation

Never bolus KCl-supplemented fluids. Mix thoroughly and use a controlled infusion pump. AAHA advises a maximum supplementation rate of 0.5 mEq/kg/hr. This tool applies that ceiling to the entered supplemental rate. Source and limits.

Reference & context

Veterinary concentration recommendations vary; 0.06 mEq/mL is a conservative peripheral irritation reference, not a universal toxicity cutoff. Added KCl only; native carrier potassium is excluded. WSAVA peripheral reference · Alternative veterinary dilution guidance

Worked math for the selected rate
    Calculation conventions

    Specified final volume: KCl mL = V × C ÷ S. Existing carrier volume: KCl mL = V × C ÷ (S − C), where C = (target − separate K rate) × weight ÷ fluid rate, S = stock concentration, and V = entered volume. Carrier potassium is intentionally excluded.

    The original Excel calculation uses the entered bag volume divided by fluid rate without adjusting for additive volume. The specified-final-volume mode reproduces that KCl amount; the existing-carrier-volume mode adjusts for the extra volume.

    Recalculate when the fluid rate or other infusions change. Preparation volumes use one decimal at or above 1, and two decimals below 1; calculations retain full precision. Delivery verification uses the displayed stock and carrier quantities. Verify measurement feasibility and use a clinician-approved dilution when needed. Catheter suitability, osmolarity, compatibility, renal function, and indication for supplementation require separate assessment.
